attacks.claim: The endpoint mapping is not equivalent. `/v2/arrivals` takes only `stop_id`, but it is listed as the replacement for the route-scoped `/v1/routes/{id}/stops/{id}` and for `/v1/predictions`, which has no stop filter. Clients migrating those calls cannot get the same results, and the parity test does not cover them.
attacks.evidence: | `GET /v2/arrivals?stop_id=…` | `/v1/stops/{id}/predictions`, `/v1/predictions`, `/v1/routes/{id}/stops/{id}` |; parity covers only "2,000 sampled stop/time pairs"

attacks.claim: The advance gates (5xx, p95, parity) are listed after "open v2 to all", so nothing gates the public opening. The deprecation headers, the 1,412-holder email and the blog post are irreversible and are all tied to launch day. A failed canary or rollback would leave v2 at 503 while v1 is already announced as deprecated. The plan does not say that these announcements wait for the gates.
attacks.evidence: "3. Publish docs and blog post; open v2 to all. 4. Advance gates: v2 5xx < 0.1%, p95 < 100 ms, parity monitor ≥ 99.9%." and "Email to all 1,412 registered key holders on launch day"

attacks.claim: Degraded mode serves the last good snapshot with no maximum staleness cutoff, and it was tested only for a 3-minute stall. The `degraded` flag and the page at 120 s mitigate this, but a long outage could still serve very old arrival times.
attacks.evidence: "responses keep serving the last good snapshot with `feed_age_seconds` set and `meta.degraded: true`"; "AVL feed paused 3 min in staging"

attacks.claim: The v2 autoscaling group has no stated maximum size or spend alarm. Per-key and per-IP limits do not bound aggregate load, because many keys can be issued.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: max instances or cost alarm for the v2 autoscaling group; "Optional free key ... raises the limit to 1,000 requests/min"

attacks.claim: Per-IP and per-key rate limiting implies request logs tying clients to stop and time, but no retention or anonymization policy is stated. The "no operator/driver identifiers" claim also has no field-level audit behind it.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: log retention for "60 requests/min per IP"; "No operator/driver identifiers are present in v1 or v2."

attacks.claim: Rollback returns 503 for all `/v2/*` traffic with no fallback to v1. It also does not reverse the deprecation signals, so clients that already migrated lose service. The plan does not name who calls the rollback or on what signal.
attacks.evidence: "Rollback: gateway route weight for `/v2/*` back to 0 (returns 503 with a link to status page)"

attacks.claim: The headline crowding, wheelchair and bike-rack fields have no stated data source or accuracy validation, yet the blog post promotes them as fact.
The blog's requested credit line differs from the mandated attribution text, and the attribution has no licence link.
attacks.evidence: "Please credit \"Metro Transit\" in your app." vs "Contains data from Metro Transit, CC BY 4.0"

attacks.claim: The isolation claim is stronger than the shared-ingestion design supports, and no shared-pipeline fault test is shown. The claim is scoped to v2 faults, so this is a wording and evidence gap.
attacks.evidence: "v2 shares the ingestion pipeline with v1 ... so a v2 fault cannot take down v1."
